prompt: Summarize this scientific methods section into a single paragraph a journalist could use, explicitly flagging any part of the methodology that limits how strongly the results can be generalized: 'Participants (n=45, convenience sample from a single university) completed a 6-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions via a mobile app. Self-reported stress levels were measured using the PSS-10 scale at baseline and post-intervention. No control group was used due to resource constraints; instead, a within-subjects pre-post design was employed.'

response_text: The study tracked 45 students from a single university who completed a six‑week, daily 10‑minute mindfulness program delivered through a mobile app, measuring their stress with the PSS‑10 questionnaire before and after the intervention; however, the convenience sampling of a modest, homogenous group (n = 45) and the absence of a control group—due to resource constraints—mean the findings are based on a within‑subjects pre‑post design and rely on self‑reported data, which **limits the extent to which the results can be generalized to broader populations or attributed solely to the mindfulness program**.
